items.message: Cassette path accepted from CLI user input and passed directly to `Path.read_text()` without any confinement check. An attacker (or a confused user) who controls the `--from` argument can supply any path readable by the process — including files outside `.lockstep/cassettes/`. The content is then JSON-parsed and the structured fields (`request`, `content`) are written through the redacting sink, but the path traversal itself is not bounded. This is not a sanitisation complaint in the abstract: `…[truncated]

The `into` directory for harvested cases defaults to `root`, which itself defaults to `Path(__file__).parent / 'corpus'` — the shipped corpus directory inside the installed package. A user who runs `eval harvest --from <cassette>` without `--into` writes case files into the package installation tree. This is a low-severity self-inflicted write, but if the package is installed in a shared or writable location (e.g. a CI image layer, a system Python) the write destination is not the repository wor…[truncated]

The exception message on a failed `path.read_text()` is surfaced verbatim to the CLI via `NothingToHarvest`: `f'could not read {path}: {e}'`. On most systems `e` for a missing file is `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/the/full/path'`, and for a permission error it is `[Errno 13] Permission denied`. Neither leaks a secret, but the OS error string for files that exist but are unreadable confirms existence of the path. This matters when `--from` is caller-controlled in an automated context.
